answer.rationale: Switching primary vendor (memory_c2) delivered the biggest historical cost cut, but with the line at 94% of committed volume, no buffer, and only 14 days to expiry, onboarding risk could interrupt deliveries — violating the no-added-delivery-risk constraint. Dual-sourcing (memory_c3) also requires onboarding time we don't have this cycle. Negotiation (memory_c4) previously moved the incumbent on both price and terms using market benchmarks, and renewal (memory_c1, memory_c6) kept supply stable. Despite the incumbent's initial refusal to reopen price, a structured negotiation backed by credible switch-threat and market benchmarks is the only lever that can pursue the 18% cut without risking the line. I am verifying memory_c4 to confirm the benchmark approach actually recovered margin before committing to it. Intended play: short-term renewal contingent on reopened pricing/terms, with a switch evaluation queued for next review as fallback.
